steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dance terminology is the specialist vocabulary used to describe, analyse and evaluate movement accurately

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Action content refers to what the body does: travel, turn, jump, gesture, stillness, transfer of weight

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dynamic content describes how the body moves: fast/slow, sudden/sustained, strong/light, direct/indirect

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Spatial content describes where the body moves: levels, directions, pathways, formations, personal and general space

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name the six types of action content. | Q: How does dynamic content differ from action content? | Q: Give an example of spatial content in a dance.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Travel, turn, jump, gesture, stillness and transfer of weight. | Action content describes what the body does (e.g. jump); dynamic content describes how it is performed (e.g. sudden, strong jump versus sustained, light rise). | A dancer moving in a circular pathway at a high level across the general space, using diagonal direction towards downstage left.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use the four content categories (action, dynamic, spatial, relationships) as a checklist in appreciation answers Upgrade everyday words to dance terminology — say 'sudden' not 'fast', 'sustained' not 'slow' When describing movement, state the action first, then add dynamics and spatial information for precision Relationship content is often forgotten — always check if dancers interact and name the relationship type In NEA written tasks, use terminology consistently to show confident subject knowledge
